newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index falls in Feb for 6th month.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index falls in Feb for 6th month.

text.p: The UK longer leading index fell for the sixth successive month in February to 91.5 from 91.8, NTC Research said.
The research group was publishing the figures for the first time after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) discontinued publication in February.

"Although all components have fallen in recent months, the downturn has been a result of sharp falls in interest rates and the yield curve," NTC said. "There was also a slight fall in the rate of growth of housing." February indices are based on partial data and are subject to revision.
The shorter leading index, which had fallen in the previous three months, rose to 99.5 in February from 98.3 in January.

"The chief cause of this rise was a significant increase in the EC/GfK consumer confidence index. Allied to an increased contribution from share prices, this was sufficient to outweight a fall in new car registrations," NTC said.

The coincident index fell to 99.1 in January from 99.9 in December, mainly due to a decreased contribution from the index of production, which outweighed increased contributions from real M0 money supply, retail sales and gross domestic product.
The lagging index fell slightly to 101.5 in January from 101.6 in December, despite increased contributions from the unemployment index, manufacturing employment and level of stocks.
"A significant decrease in the contribution of engineering industries' orders on hand was the principal reason for this fall," NTC said.
NTC said it used an identical methodology to that previously used by the ONS in calculating the indicators.
